name: Net
overview: The Bible uses the image of a net both literally and figuratively to convey themes of entrapment and divine sovereignty. Nets are described as tools for catching fish and wild animals, as well as traps hidden in pits or set for birds and the poor, illustrating the dangers of sin and the snares that can entangle the unwary (Psalms 9:15; Psalms 10:9). At the same time, Scripture acknowledges God's control over these snares, as He can both surround and rescue His people from the net of adversity or judgment (Job 19:6; Psalms 25:15). The craftsmanship of nets, such as those of checker work mentioned in 1 Kings 7:17, also reflects the detailed design behind these symbolic traps.
